product_name: U.S. Independent Retail Pharmacy Facility Directory 2026
one_liner: Complete CSV of independent community, compounding, specialty, and LTC pharmacy FACILITIES (~19,400 NCPA independents after chain exclusion) — with NPI (Type 2), DEA registration, NABP number, state license status, pharmacist-in-charge, owner-of-record, and services-offered flags. The chain-exclusion filter (CVS/Walgreens/Rite Aid/Walmart/Kroger removed) is a wedge no existing $1,500-$6,000/yr vendor offers.
audience: Pharmaceutical wholesalers and distributors (Cardinal Health, AmerisourceBergen/Cencora, McKesson, Morris & Dickson, HD Smith) recruiting independent pharmacy accounts — each facility represents $300K-$2M/year in wholesale GMV; pharmacy management system (PMS) and POS vendors (PioneerRx, BestRx, ComputerRx, Liberty Pharmacy Systems, Micro Merchant Systems, Rx30, Datascan) selling $300-$2,000/month SaaS to independent sites; pharmacy automation and robotics vendors (Parata, ScriptPro, RxSafe, Omnicell, BD Rowa) selling $50K-$500K dispensing systems; PSAO (Pharmacy Services Administrative Organizations like AmerisourceBergen's Elevate Provider Network, McKesson's Health Mart, Cardinal's Leader, IPC, EPIC Pharmacies) recruiting member pharmacies; specialty pharmacy accreditors (URAC, ACHC) prospecting; compounding pharmacy supply (PCCA, Medisca, Letco Medical); pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) for credentialing and network outreach; 340B contract pharmacy program enrollers; pharmacy E&O / professional liability insurance brokers (Pharmacists Mutual); pharmacy financing and acquisition advisors (M&A is hot — corporate chains and PE rollups actively buy independents).
core_fields: Services offered (retail / compounding / specialty / LTC / mail-order)
Source URL (state board / DEA / NABP / CMS NPPES)
estimated_row_count_rationale: ~88,000 total US pharmacies (NABP 2025). ~19,400 independent community pharmacies (NCPA). ~7,500 specialty pharmacies. ~5,500 compounding pharmacies (PCAB/ACHC accredited subset is ~600). Top-20 chains own ~40% of all retail dispensing sites — the remaining 60%+ is the addressable independent universe. Buyer LTV by segment: wholesaler account = $300K-$2M/year GMV; PMS software = $3.6K-$24K/year SaaS; automation = $50K-$500K capex one-time; PSAO membership = $2K-$10K/year fees per pharmacy; PBM credentialing services = $5K-$25K/year; pharmacy M&A advisory = $50K-$500K per transaction.
pricing_rationale: State-level CSVs at $49-$79 each. Fields: pharmacy DBA name, legal entity name, NABP number, DEA registration, NPI (Type 2), street address, phone, owner-of-record name, pharmacist-in-charge, license status, services offered (retail / compounding / specialty / LTC / mail-order), Medicare/Medicaid enrollment flag. Top-5-state bundle (CA + TX + FL + NY + PA) at $199. National independents-only bundle (~19,400 records) at $349 vs. competitor $1,500-$6,000 subscriptions. Add-ons: '340B contract pharmacies only' filter SKU ($99), 'compounding pharmacies only' filter SKU ($99) — both are higher-LTV buyer segments.
source_url: State Boards of Pharmacy facility license registries (all 50 states + DC, distinct from individual pharmacist licensure); NABP (National Association of Boards of Pharmacy) e-Profile / Pharmacy Search public lookup; DEA Diversion Control Active Controlled Substance Registrant lookup (public FOIA-released file); CMS NPPES (Type 2 organizational NPIs filed under pharmacy taxonomy codes 333600000X and subcodes); CMS Medicare Part D Prescriber and Pharmacy file (Medicare-enrolled pharmacies); HRSA 340B OPAIS covered entity / contract pharmacy registry; USP <797>/<800> compounding pharmacy accreditation registries (PCAB / ACHC); State Secretary of State business registry cross-reference for ownership entities
data_freshness_requirement: Semi-annual updates. Pharmacy facility licenses renew annually or biennially. Closures and ownership changes ~6-9% per year (driven by chain-acquisition rollups, PBM reimbursement pressure, and retirements). DEA registration changes flagged via DEA Controlled Substance Registrant file updates.
compliance_notes: PASS. All fields sourced from state pharmacy board public license registries (public record under state pharmacy practice acts), NABP public profile, DEA public registrant lookup (FOIA-released), and CMS NPPES (public per HIPAA — organizational NPI is public). Pharmacist-in-charge name is public per state board records. No patient data, no PHI, no consumer PII. DEA registration numbers are part of the public DEA Diversion Control registrant file. Source attribution per state board URL and DEA/NABP/CMS URLs.
distribution_channels: LinkedIn DM outreach to PMS vendors (PioneerRx/BestRx/ComputerRx), PSAOs, and pharma wholesaler account teams
